description: Central store-and-reuse Scrydex pricing orchestrator + sync engine rewiring + backfill pilot. Adds scrydex-pricing.service.ts (the single writer owning the freshness gate, first-pull trend backfill, and SyncLog credit metering), rewires sync-cards.service.ts price fallbacks (TCGdex->PokeWallet for Pokemon, apitcg catalog + BerryWallet pricing for One Piece, stamping Card.game/source), and rewrites scripts/scrydex-backfill.ts to defer entirely to the orchestrator. Depends on FEAT-001 (schema + both clients + exported ApiTcgProduct).
steps: NEW src/lib/services/scrydex-pricing.service.ts (design §3.6): export `SCRYDEX_STALE_MS = 24*60*60*1000` with a `ponytail:` comment naming the 24h ceiling + upgrade path, and `SCRYDEX_CREDITS_PER_CALL = 1` with a `ponytail:` provisional comment (pilot measures real cost). `pullAndStoreScrydexPrice(card:{id;externalId;name;number;game;scrydexId?;setName?;setCode?}, opts?:{force?}): Promise<{pulled:boolean;credits:number}>`: (1) FRESHNESS GATE unless opts.force — findFirst SyncLog where {job:'scrydex_history',cardId} orderBy ranAt desc; if ranAt within SCRYDEX_STALE_MS -> return {pulled:false,credits:0}, no HTTP, no row (gate reads SyncLog.ranAt NOT CurrentPrice — a graded-only/no-raw card still writes a SyncLog so it is throttled). (2) PULL: if card.scrydexId cached -> fetchScrydexCardById(scrydexId,game); else resolveScrydexCard({name,number,setName,setCode,game}) and on success write back Card.scrydexId; null/throw -> write SyncLog(status:'failed',credits:0,error) and return {pulled:false,credits:0}. (3) PERSIST from pickRawPrice: INSERT PricingHistory {cardId,priceMarket,priceLow,source:'scrydex',currency,variant,condition,recordedAt:now} via createMany({skipDuplicates:true}); UPSERT CurrentPrice keyed [cardId,source,currency,variant,condition] with source:DataSource.SCRYDEX. (4) FIRST-PULL TREND BACKFILL only (count existing scrydex/scrydex-trend PricingHistory rows for [cardId,variant,condition] before step 3's insert): up to 3 points source:'scrydex-trend' at now-{1,7,14}d with price = market - trends.days_{1,7,14}.price_change (absolute delta subtraction); skip null/missing deltas; PricingHistory ONLY (never CurrentPrice — enum has no scrydex-trend member). (5) METER: SyncLog(job:'scrydex_history',cardId,status:'ok',credits:SCRYDEX_CREDITS_PER_CALL) on each successful fetch; backfill adds no extra credits. This module is the ONLY place the gate + first-pull invariant + normalization live (centralised writer).

sync-cards.service.ts (design §4) (a): thread the Game through upsertCard — syncOneSet already knows game:'pokemon'|'onepiece'; map to the Prisma Game enum and pass game + source into upsertCard which writes BOTH in the create AND update branches: Pokemon(TCGdex) -> game=POKEMON, source=DataSource.TCGDEX; One Piece(apitcg) -> game=ONE_PIECE, source=DataSource.TCGDEX (NO enum expansion). Preserve all load-bearing WHY comments (NFR-9).

sync-cards.service.ts (b): the Pokemon price-gap call site in listPokemonCardsInSet (~line 427) changes `fetchPokemonCardPrice(c.id)` -> `fetchPokemonCardPrice(c.name)` (the rewritten accessor is name-based GET /search?q=<name>). Keep the surrounding isActive guard + `await sleep(REQUEST_DELAY_MS)` throttle. Add the known-imprecision comment (name-based last-resort gap fill; Scrydex refines by name+number+set later).

sync-cards.service.ts (c): replace the PokeWallet One Piece CATALOG path with two thin apitcg fetchers reusing the exported ApiTcgProduct (header x-api-key: APITCG_API_KEY). `listOnePieceSets(): Promise<SyncSetInput[]>` GET https://api.apitcg.com/api/one-piece/sets, Zod ApiTcgSetsResponseSchema, map sourceSetId=_id (the /products set= slug), name, series='One Piece Card Game', releaseDate; empty/parse-fail -> throw NoResultsError (caught by safelyListSets). `listOnePieceCardsInSet(sourceSetId): Promise<SyncCardInput[]>` GET https://api.apitcg.com/api/products?tcg=one-piece&set={sourceSetId}&limit=500, Zod ApiTcgProductsResponseSchema with images as ARRAY, map externalId=product.code (Bandai code; fallback String(_id)), name, number=attributes?.Number??code, rarity, types=parseOnePieceAttrs(attributes), `const img=product.images?.[0]; imageUrl=img?.large??img?.medium??img?.small??null`, marketPrice=markets?.tcgplayer?.prices?.market??null; drop products with no code/name; empty valid set -> throw NoResultsError.

sync-cards.service.ts (d): One Piece price GAP fill — per synced set, after building the apitcg card list, derive the Bandai set code from the first card's externalId.split('-')[0], call fetchOnePieceSetPrices(setCode) ONCE, and fill card.marketPrice from priceMap.get(card.externalId) ONLY where the apitcg tcgplayer price was null (externalId === PokeWallet card_number, no normalization).

sync-cards.service.ts (e): after the catalog upsert, call pullAndStoreScrydexPrice for active cards (both games) to grow the real history series on the daily cadence — gated by the freshness window and bounded by the RUN_BUDGET_MS deadline check; additive, never blocks catalog. Preserve smart-sync active-only repricing, STALE_AFTER_DAYS window, interleaveByGame, RUN_BUDGET_MS budget, fetch-before-upsert, and all load-bearing comments (AC-8).

REWRITE scripts/scrydex-backfill.ts (design §8): import pullAndStoreScrydexPrice (not the deleted fetchPriceHistory). Select exactly 10 cards with userCollections:{some:{}}, take:10, select {id,externalId,name,number,game,scrydexId,set:{select:{name:true}}}. For each: await pullAndStoreScrydexPrice(card); await sleep(3000) between (Cloudflare). ZERO direct Prisma writes (DELETE the 'Near Mint'/'Normal' literals + inline createMany). Sum returned credits; print total + per-card ok/skip/fail summary. Idempotent via the freshness gate. In FEAT findings, record the MEASURED credit figure and update SCRYDEX_CREDITS_PER_CALL if it differs from 1.
acceptance_criteria: A Scrydex price pull writes one PricingHistory row (source='scrydex') and upserts one CurrentPrice row keyed by cardId+source+currency+variant+condition (AC-9).

A first pull optionally writes up to 3 source='scrydex-trend' points from days_1/7/14 deltas (market - price_change), distinguishable from fresh snapshots, with none written beyond trend-derived points and none to CurrentPrice (AC-10).

A re-pull within SCRYDEX_STALE_MS is skipped (no Scrydex call, no row) gated on the newest SyncLog(job='scrydex_history',cardId).ranAt; a pull outside the window proceeds; the window is a named constant with a ponytail comment (AC-11).
Every Scrydex pull writes a SyncLog(job='scrydex_history',cardId,credits,status) row on both ok and failed attempts (AC-12).

The sync prices One Piece via BerryWallet and Pokemon active cards via PokeWallet only when TCGdex/apitcg has no price; One Piece catalog still comes from apitcg; upserts stamp Card.game+source; smart-sync/staleness/interleave/wall-clock budget are unchanged (AC-8).

scripts/scrydex-backfill.ts processes exactly 10 collection-active cards, persists via pullAndStoreScrydexPrice (zero direct writes), logs total + per-card credit usage, is idempotent, and respects the freshness gate (AC-18).
verification: npm run type-check  (sync call-site now passes c.name; orchestrator + apitcg fetchers compile)
npm run build  (next build compiles the sync + new service module)
findings:
ORCHESTRATOR (NEW src/lib/services/scrydex-pricing.service.ts): the SINGLE writer. Exports SCRYDEX_STALE_MS=24h (ponytail comment: ceiling = no intraday refresh, upgrade path = per-card volatility windows) and SCRYDEX_CREDITS_PER_CALL=1 (ponytail: provisional). pullAndStoreScrydexPrice({id,externalId,name,number,game,scrydexId?,setName?,setCode?},{force?}) does: (1) freshness gate reads newest SyncLog(job='scrydex_history',cardId).ranAt — NOT CurrentPrice — so a graded-only/no-raw card still writes a SyncLog and is throttled 24h (AC-11); (2) pull by cached scrydexId -> fetchScrydexCardById else resolveScrydexCard, writes back Card.scrydexId on resolve (best-effort, unique-collision swallowed since it is just a cache), null/throw -> SyncLog(status='failed',credits:0) + return (AC-12); (3) persist from pickRawPrice: PricingHistory createMany(skipDuplicates) source='scrydex' + CurrentPrice upsert source=DataSource.SCRYDEX keyed [cardId,source,currency,variant,condition] (AC-9); (4) first-pull-only trend backfill via exported pure buildTrendBackfill(market,trends,now) — count of existing scrydex/scrydex-trend rows for [cardId,variant,condition] taken BEFORE the step-3 insert, up to 3 points source='scrydex-trend' at now-{1,7,14}d = market - days_{1,7,14}.price_change (absolute delta), skips null/non-finite/<=0, PricingHistory ONLY never CurrentPrice (AC-10); (5) meter SyncLog(status='ok',credits:SCRYDEX_CREDITS_PER_CALL) once per successful fetch regardless of raw presence; trend points add no credits.

SYNC REWIRE (sync-cards.service.ts): (a) threaded PrismaGame through syncOneSet->upsertCard; upsertCard now stamps game + source=DataSource.TCGDEX in BOTH create and update branches (Pokemon=POKEMON, One Piece=ONE_PIECE; no enum expansion — per-price provenance lives on CurrentPrice.source). (b) listPokemonCardsInSet price gap-fill call changed fetchPokemonCardPrice(c.id)->fetchPokemonCardPrice(c.name) and read price?.market (new OnePiecePrice shape); isActive guard + sleep(REQUEST_DELAY_MS) preserved; known-imprecision comment added. (c) DELETED the PokeWallet One Piece CATALOG path (fetchPWOnePieceSets/fetchPWOnePieceCards imports gone); added two thin apitcg fetchers reusing header x-api-key:APITCG_API_KEY with Zod ApiTcgSetsResponseSchema + ApiTcgProductsResponseSchema (images ARRAY), mapping externalId=product.code (fallback String(_id)), number=attributes.Number??code, img=images[0].large??medium??small??null, marketPrice=markets.tcgplayer.prices.market??null; empty/parse-fail -> NoResultsError (caught by safelyListSets). A `satisfies Partial<Record<keyof ApiTcgProduct,undefined>>` field-pin ties the parser's field names to the exported ApiTcgProduct interface so the two consumers cannot drift (finding #2). (d) One Piece price gap fill: setCode derived from collected[0].externalId.split('-')[0], fetchOnePieceSetPrices(setCode) once per set, priceMap.get(card.externalId) fills marketPrice ONLY where apitcg tcgplayer price was null. (e) after catalog upsert, loop active cards (both games), findUnique the DB card (id/externalId/name/number/game/scrydexId), call pullAndStoreScrydexPrice (setName=set.name; setCode=externalId prefix for One Piece only), bounded by the SAME RUN_BUDGET_MS deadline + sleep(REQUEST_DELAY_MS). Preserved: smart-sync active-only, STALE_AFTER_DAYS, interleaveByGame, RUN_BUDGET_MS, fetch-before-upsert, and all load-bearing WHY comments (AC-8). Removed now-unused pickPokemonMarketPrice import.

BACKFILL (scripts/scrydex-backfill.ts REWRITTEN): imports pullAndStoreScrydexPrice (deleted fetchPriceHistory import + the inline createMany + 'Near Mint'/'Normal' literals). Selects exactly 10 userCollections:{some:{}} take:10 with {id,externalId,name,number,game,scrydexId,set:{name}}; per card await pullAndStoreScrydexPrice then sleep(3000) (Cloudflare); ZERO direct Prisma writes; sums returned credits and prints total + per-card ok/skip/fail + per-pull cost; idempotent via the freshness gate (AC-18).

MEASURED CREDIT FIGURE: NOT measured in this step. The pilot requires a LIVE Scrydex run (credit cost + Cloudflare-hang risk on rapid calls, env-constrained MEDIUM-risk live action) which is intentionally a separate operator-run step, not part of FEAT-002's build-only verification (type-check/lint/build). SCRYDEX_CREDITS_PER_CALL therefore stays at its provisional 1 with its ponytail comment; the rewritten backfill script prints the measured per-pull figure when the operator runs `tsx scripts/scrydex-backfill.ts` live, and the constant should be updated then if it differs from 1. Flagged for the user-testing checklist.

VERIFICATION: npm run type-check PASS (exit 0 — the FEAT-001 stale sync call-site errors are resolved: fetchPokemonCardPrice now takes c.name, One Piece catalog uses apitcg not the deleted PokeWallet catalog fns). npm run lint PASS (exit 0). npm run build PASS (prisma generate + next build compiled successfully, 38 routes, no type errors). No DB writes performed in this step.
